colors.instruction: Return one or two distinct color families, or [Multicolor] alone. Assess the target garment itself, including meaningful prints and panels; ignore lighting, skin, background and separate styling garments. More than two discernible color families or an explicit multicolor design means Multicolor. Do not rank colors by dominance.

values.White: White, off-white, ivory, cream and ecru.
values.Blue: Blue shades including navy, midnight blue, cobalt, indigo and turquoise.
values.Red: Red including burgundy, maroon, bordeaux, crimson and scarlet.
values.Green: Green including olive, khaki and emerald.
values.Pink: Pink including fuchsia and rose pink.
values.Purple: Purple including violet, lilac, lavender and mauve.
values.Multicolor: More than two color families, or an explicitly multicolored design; must appear alone.

pattern.instruction: Return one value describing the target garment design as a whole. Plain means Solid. Ribbing, melange, fabric texture, seams and small construction trims do not by themselves create a pattern. A localized decorative print still counts: classify its actual motif. Do not classify the whole garment as Striped merely because the collar or cuff has stripe trim. For multiple substantial different pattern families, choose Other.

values.Solid: No decorative print or recognizable patterned motif; plain, ribbed or heathered material can be Solid.
values.Striped: A recognizable repeated stripe design, horizontal, vertical or diagonal, including broad stripes.
values.Plaid: Checks, tartan, gingham or another repeated intersecting grid.
values.Floral: Recognizable flowers, leaves or botanical motifs, whether printed or embroidered.
values.Camo: A camouflage design, including stylized camouflage.
values.Animal Print: A pattern imitating animal markings or skin, e.g. leopard spots, zebra stripes or snakeskin; a picture of an animal is not automatically Animal Print.
values.Polka Dot: A recognizable repeated pattern of dots.
values.Other: Graphics, lettering, logos, abstract motifs, fruit prints, color blocking without a repeated stripe pattern, mixed substantial pattern families, or another design outside the specific labels.

sleeve_length.instruction: Return one value for the garment sleeve itself, not an undershirt, gloves, or sleeves rolled up for styling. Consider the original sleeve endpoint. If the design has genuinely incompatible sleeve lengths and no single label describes it, outside_schema is permitted.

values.Sleeveless: No sleeve extends over the upper arm; shoulder straps are not sleeves.
values.Short Sleeve: A sleeve covering part of the upper arm and ending above the elbow, including cap sleeves.
values.Three-Quarter Sleeve: A sleeve ending below the elbow and before the wrist. In this project, an explicit cropped sleeve description also maps here.
values.Long Sleeve: A full-length sleeve reaching the wrist or beyond.

neckline.instruction: Return one value for the front neckline of the target garment. A low back does not make the front a V-Neck. Do not classify a separate garment worn underneath.

values.Crewneck: A relatively close, rounded neckline at the base of the neck.
values.Scoop Neck: A visibly lower and wider rounded or U-shaped neckline.
values.V-Neck: A front neckline with sides converging to a V-shaped point.
values.High Neck: A neckline rising up the neck: turtleneck, mock neck, funnel neck or similar; an ordinary crewneck is not High Neck.
values.Collared: An actual garment collar, including shirt, spread, point or band/stand collar; distinguish it from a knitted high neck.
values.Other: A neckline outside the offered labels, such as boat, square, sweetheart, cowl, straight-across or asymmetric. A collar belongs here when Collared is not an offered label.

fit.instruction: Return one value for the intended fit of the target garment, considering torso ease and shoulder construction together. Do not infer Slim just from a slim model, or Oversized just from garment length. Explicit garment fit descriptions are useful evidence.

values.Slim: Close-fitting through the torso with little ease; fitted, form-fitting or body-hugging.
values.Regular: Conventional ease, neither close-fitting nor deliberately loose.
values.Oversized: Deliberately loose, relaxed, boxy or oversized through the torso; not merely a normal fit on a slender model.

length.instruction: Return one value for the body length of the top, not sleeve length. Use untucked views when available. A tucked hem alone does not establish a cropped design.

values.Cropped: A deliberately shortened top ending around or above the natural waist, rather than reaching the usual hip area.
values.Regular: A conventional top length reaching around the waistband or hips, without an intentionally extended body.
values.Longline: An intentionally elongated body extending clearly below the usual hip length, toward the upper thigh or beyond.

dress_silhouette.instruction: Return one value for the overall body-and-skirt outline, not just whether the bodice is tight. A fitted bodice with a clearly flared skirt belongs to A-Line.

values.Fitted: The dress closely follows the torso and hips, with a bodycon or similarly close outline.
values.Straight: A predominantly straight or column-like outline, including shift dresses; it need not be tight.
values.A-Line: The skirt noticeably widens from the waist or upper body toward the hem, including fit-and-flare.
values.Other: A silhouette not adequately described above, such as pronounced cocoon, balloon, mermaid or irregular draped construction.

dress_type.instruction: Return a nonempty list of distinct types. Multiple types are allowed only when the target genuinely combines them. Other must appear alone. A lining or a separate slip underneath does not make the target a Slip dress. A belt alone does not make a Wrap dress. T-Shirt Dress does not imply Shirt Dress.

values.Slip: A slip/camisole-style dress, typically with lingerie-like construction and shoulder straps.
values.Shirt Dress: A dress constructed like a shirt, typically with a placket, shirt detailing or collar.
values.Wrap: A dress with actual overlapping wrap-front construction, usually secured at the side or waist.
values.Sweater Dress: A dress with sweater-like knitted construction.
values.Sweatshirt Dress: A dress with sweatshirt or hoodie construction, such as French terry or fleece and sweatshirt detailing.
values.T-Shirt Dress: A dress with a jersey T-shirt construction extended into a dress.
values.Other: A dress not matching the offered specific types.

strap_style.instruction: Return one value for the upper-body and shoulder construction. Distinctive construction takes precedence over an ordinary configuration; use Other for an unlisted combination that cannot be represented faithfully by one label. The mere presence of sleeves does not establish a standard shoulder construction.

values.Standard: An ordinary sleeveless upper construction with two shoulder straps or two conventional shoulder sections, without the special constructions listed below.
values.Standard Sleeved: A conventional sleeved upper construction with covered shoulders, without off-shoulder, one-shoulder, halter or other special construction.
values.Racerback: Shoulder straps or back panels converge into a central athletic Y/T-shaped back; ordinary crossed straps are not necessarily racerback.
values.Halter: The upper garment is supported around or behind the neck, rather than by two ordinary shoulder straps.
values.One-Shoulder: An asymmetric upper construction supported on or covering one shoulder.
values.Strapless: A strap-free upper construction with neither shoulder nor neck support. Do not infer absence of sleeves solely from this label.
values.Off-Shoulder: An upper edge sitting below the shoulders and exposing both shoulder tops; do not confuse with a low neckline that retains ordinary shoulder support.
values.Other: Another upper construction, e.g. a distinct crossed-back arrangement or a combination not represented by one offered label.

strap_width.instruction: Return one value for the actual shoulder-support fabric, not the neckline binding. Look at front and back views. A sleeveless garment with broad shoulder sections counts as having broad straps for this taxonomy.

values.Spaghetti: Very thin cord-like or narrow ribbon straps.
values.Wide: Clearly broad straps or broad shoulder sections; not merely thicker than a spaghetti strap.
values.Other: Intermediate-width straps, different widths on the two sides, or another width configuration outside the offered labels.
values.Not Applicable: Use only for a strapless upper construction or, where supported by this category, a conventional sleeved upper construction. Do not use it merely because straps are difficult to see.
